// era.js.txt — SCANNED, NEVER RUN. One site per gated syntax feature, so that
// every `kind_needs` row in facts/js-env.rofl is verified by something the
// scanner really emits rather than by the table agreeing with itself.
//
// THE `.txt` TAIL IS LOAD-BEARING, for the same reason it is on
// test/fixtures/js-call/shapes.ts.txt: tsconfig's include covers `test/**`
// and a fixture whose job is to hold one of everything cannot also be a file
// the project compiles and runs.
//
// It is a SEPARATE CORPUS from test/fixtures/js-call on purpose. That corpus
// answers a different question — which call edges the runtime really takes —
// and its counts are pinned test by test; growing it to exercise `for-of`
// would move numbers that have nothing to do with syntax eras.
import defaultExport from './other.js';
import { named } from './other.js';
import * as everything from './other.js';
export * from './other.js';

const arrow = (n) => n + 1;

// DESTRUCTURING, ES2015, added 2026-09-08 with `object_pattern`. One site here
// because `feature_unexercised[audit]` demands one: a `kind_needs` row the era
// corpus never produces is a table agreeing with itself, which is what this
// file exists to prevent.
const { named: renamed } = { named: 1 };

// THREE MORE, 2026-09-08, with the twenty-three kinds the vocabulary took on.
// All three are ES2020 or earlier, which is why they are HERE and class fields
// are not: this file is asserted to fail es2020 for EXACTLY ONE reason and that
// reason is an operator, so a 2022 feature would have made that assertion
// two-valued — the same care era-position.js was split out for.
const big = 1n;                        // bigint, ES2020
function withTarget() { return new.target; }   // meta_property, ES2015
export * as everythingElse from './other.js';  // namespace_reexport, ES2020

function* counter() { yield 1; yield 2; }

class Base { greet() { return 'base'; } }
class Sub extends Base { greet() { return super.greet() + '!'; } }

const shorthand = {
  method(n) { return n; },
  tag: 'plain',
};

function templates(who) {
  return `hello ${who}` + String.raw`raw ${who}`;
}

function loop(xs) {
  let total = 0;
  for (const x of xs) { total += x; }
  return total;
}

async function fetchThing(url) {
  const mod = await import(url);
  return mod?.value ?? mod?.get?.();
}

// THE KIND IS NOT ALWAYS THE FEATURE. Every line below is a `binary_expression`,
// a `logical_expression` or an `assignment_expression` — kinds that are as old
// as the language — and the era each one belongs to is carried by the OPERATOR
// attribute and by nothing else. `attr_needs` in facts/js-env.rofl is the
// refinement that makes these visible; without it a file using `??=` reads as
// pure es5.
// TWO STRING LITERALS WHOSE VALUE IS AN OPERATOR. `attr_needs` joins on the
// KEY as well as the value, and without these two lines that join is
// unmeasured: no other attribute in the corpus happens to carry `**` or `??`,
// so a rule that forgot the key would be indistinguishable from one that
// keeps it. Measured — the mutant that drops the key SURVIVED until these
// existed, which is the difference between a gate and a decoration.
const powerSign = '**';
const nullishSign = '??';

function operators(a, b) {
  let acc = a ** b;      // ES2016
  acc ??= b;             // ES2021
  acc ||= a;             // ES2021
  acc &&= b;             // ES2021
  return acc + (a ?? b); // ?? is ES2020, + is not
}

export { arrow, counter, Sub, shorthand, templates, loop, fetchThing, operators, powerSign, nullishSign, defaultExport, named, everything };
